plan.title: design-critique v1 vehicle — locked decisions (discuss strategy, 2026-08-20)

narratives.Context: Phase 1 of the design-critique motion (the judgment gate) is locked separately as ADR-005 and is vehicle-invariant. This discuss session locked where Phases 2-5 scaffolding lives: the critic charter/brief template, envelope and ceiling discipline, the variant table (refutation/open/panel), and the synthesis format (method column, decorrelation, Current-shape conformance). Evidence base: the #3383/#3462/#3547 exemplar arcs, the Pass-4 detection test, the naive-orchestrator run on #3570-#3572, and the fresh-critic critique of the skill outline on #3434.
narratives.LockedDecisions: D1 — VEHICLE IS A HYBRID: contract doc as sole normative SoT + copyable brief template + thin router skill + ADR-005 gate. Homes: content/contracts/design-critique.md (charter, variant table, envelope/ceiling rules, synthesis format — locked by a content-contract test per the deterministic-questions.md #767 precedent); content/templates/design-critique-brief.md (dispatch envelope skeleton with forbidden-inputs list, per the agent-prompt-preamble.md precedent); content/skills/deft-directive-design-critique/SKILL.md (entry point ONLY: triggers, five stops as one-liners pointing into the contract, zero normative content). WHY: the naive-orchestrator run (#3570-#3572) proved prose carries behavior but issue threads are not durable product surfaces — the voluntary path needs a shipped entry point; contracts+tests are the drift-resistant home (#3547 corpus rot); each surface carries exactly the one thing its type is good at (gate=obligation, contract=rules, template=artifact, skill=trigger). ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED: (a) contract doc + template with no skill — rejected: no durable entry for the voluntary critique path once #3434 closes; 'see issue 3434' is not a product surface. (b) thin skill as SoT with rules in the skill body — rejected: two-surface normative drift is the probe disease (#3547 defect 3: skill and strategy diverged for two months). (c) strategy in the strategies pack — rejected: the strategy family is chaining-gate preparatory work hanging off interview; this motion hangs off triage. D2 — THINNESS IS MECHANICALLY ENFORCED, NOT ASPIRATIONAL: a content-contract test caps the skill (~80 lines, probe_skill.test.ts 150-line precedent), asserts every path the skill names resolves (the #3547 pointer-rot lesson), and asserts required pointer strings into the contract. WHY: prose size preferences erode exactly as the prose gate eroded — each addition individually reasonable; 'very small' must be a recorded, enforced property. ALTERNATIVE: prose guidance only — rejected: the arc's root cause is that omission-shaped and erosion-shaped rules do not survive as prose. D3 — CONSUMER PARITY CONFIRMED BEFORE LOCK: packages/content package.json ships files:**/*; content/ contains contracts/, templates/, skills/; deposit copies the whole content-package tree into .deft/core/ (deposit/resolve-content.ts); gate is opt-in per-project plan.policy.judgmentGates with verify:judgment-gates shipped via the canonical .deft/core/Taskfile.yml, advisory by default; N=1 default and the decorrelation rule's primary-source fallback cover single-model consumers. Known conditions: consumer visibility requires a release (standing deposit/release close condition, applies to every option equally); the write-back FIELD home depends on #1423 landing — the label mirror works today.
narratives.DeferredDecisions: DISPATCH BEHAVIOR (the skill actually spawning critics rather than scaffold-with-stops): undecided, deliberately. Not a graduation lock — no end-product path is decided (#2899 table: Graduation requires a decided Later; this is an open question with justification). Revisit trigger: a second consumer or orchestrator demands auto-dispatch (#1702 evidence-of-need). Until then the skill drafts envelopes and stops; the operator dispatches.
narratives.RejectedPermanently: Strategy-pack vehicle (option 3). Re-proposing requires explicit unlock with justification per the discuss decision-locking contract.
